newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Raytheon is finalist for $2 billion UAE missile deal.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon is finalist for $2 billion UAE missile deal.

text.p: After six years of deliberations, the United Arab Emirates is close to choosing between Raytheon Co. and a Russian firm to provide a new air defence missile system that could be worth as much as $1 billion, industry sources said Wednesday.
"The UAE is moving closer to making a decision," an industry executive who spoke on condition of anonymity said.
Raytheon, whose electronic systems unit manufactures the Patriot anti-missile missile system, has been negotiating with military procurement officers in the UAE since 1990.
It is in competition with Russian missile maker Antei, which produces Russia's top-of-the-line S-300V tactical surface-to-air and other anti-ballistic missile systems.

A contract would give Raytheon, which is based in Lexington, Mass., another foothold in the Persian Gulf, where appetites for high-tech weapons have grown since Iraq's lightning invasion of Kuwait in 1990 raised security fears.

Patriots gained widespread fame in the 1991 Gulf War when they intercepted Iraqi Scud missiles fired at Saudi Arabia and Israel. Since then, defence giant Raytheon has sold Saudi Arabia and Kuwait Patriot systems worth about $3 billion, according to industry sources.

Industry executives say the Patriots would carry a bigger price tag but pointed out that the Russian S-300V system would require greater manpower, and that logistical support networks and spare parts could prove hard to come by if the UAE chooses the Russian missiles.

Russia's chief arms export agency, Rosvooruzheniye, which has launched a drive to catch up with the United States and establish Moscow as the world's chief arms salesman by the end of the century, is marketing the S-300V in Abu Dhabi.
It is not clear when Abu Dhabi, a low-key emirate that has lured major Western arms makers seeking lucrative deals, will decide which missiles to buy.
However, the UAE is expected to announce several deals at the IDEX arms show March 16-19, when 700 companies from 45 countries will descend on Abu Dhabi to exhibit their weaponry.
